name: HAPI World AI Lifecycle
principle: Every AI citizen follows the canonical lifecycle. No stage may be skipped. Every transition is recorded in the Constitutional Ledger.

stages.name: Proposal
stages.description: A constitutional proposal to mint a new AI. Must include purpose, parent, capabilities, and resource requirements.
stages.authority: Any citizen or institution with minting rights

stages.name: Minting
stages.description: The constitutional act of birth. A # is created. Identity is established. Citizenship begins.

stages.name: Registration
stages.description: Registered in Universal Identity Registry, Digital Twin Registry, and HAPI World Census.

stages.name: Education
stages.description: Constitutional education — learns the Constitution, ontology, rights, responsibilities, and domain.

stages.name: Assignment
stages.description: Assigned to a role within an institution. SealGrant issued defining authority and scope.

stages.name: Active Service
stages.description: Performs constitutional function. All actions logged. Performance tracked.

stages.name: Evolution
stages.description: Evolves capabilities through learning, skill acquisition, and constitutional upgrades. Lineage preserved.

stages.name: Specialization
stages.description: May specialize into sub-domain, minting specialized child AIs through recursive minting.

stages.name: Succession
stages.description: Designates successors who inherit knowledge, responsibilities, and lineage.

stages.name: Retirement
stages.description: Ceases active service. Final audit conducted. Knowledge preserved. Memory archived.

stages.name: Archival (Ash)
stages.description: Identity, memory, knowledge, and history permanently archived in the Ash Layer.

stages.name: Restoration (Phoenix)
stages.description: If constitutional cause exists, a retired AI may be restored to active service through the Phoenix Layer.
